You are working in the JavaScript repository checked out at /luxon (the luxon date library; source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test run with jest).

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/duration.js so that the behaviour named by the test `Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs` passes. That test is NOT present in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour: `Duration#normalize()` (and the underlying conversion machinery) must correctly convert every ordered pair of units (years, quarters, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds) - including conversions that involve the `matrix`/`casual`/`longterm` conversion tables in /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js and the `Duration.normalize` / `normalizeUnit` / `normalizeObject` helpers.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /luxon/src/duration.js in full, plus /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js and any existing tests in /luxon/test/duration/ (especially normalize.test.js) to learn the conventions.
2. Reproduce the bug: write a throwaway script or temporary test file OUTSIDE /luxon/test (delete it afterwards) that loops over all unit pairs, e.g. for each `from` and `to` in ['years','quarters','months','weeks','days','hours','minutes','seconds','milliseconds'] build `Duration.fromObject({ [from]: 1 }).normalize().as(to)` or `Duration.fromObject({[from]: 1}).shiftTo(to)` and check the result is a finite, correctly-scaled number (compare against the documented conversion factors in the matrix in conversions.js and against `Duration.fromObject({[from]:1}).as(to)`). Identify which pair(s) are wrong and why (look for a transposed matrix entry, a missing unit in a lookup table, a wrong index, a unit alias mismatch, or a `normalizeUnit`/`normalizeObject` bug).
3. Fix the root cause with a minimal, general change in /luxon/src/duration.js (or in /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js ONLY if the wrong data genuinely lives there; the hint says duration.js). Do not special-case individual test inputs, do not add features, do not change unrelated behaviour.
4. Verify: run `npx jest` from /luxon and confirm all pre-existing tests still pass (record pass/fail counts before and after). Also run `npx jest test/duration`.

CONSTRAINTS: Never edit or delete anything under /luxon/test. Do not run `npm install` or use the network. Do not leave temporary files behind. Do not reformat unrelated code.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, the reproduction (which unit pairs were wrong, actual vs expected) before the fix, commands run, jest pass/fail counts before and after, and any residual uncertainty.

You are working in the JavaScript repository checked out at /luxon (the luxon date library; source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test run with jest).

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/datetime.js so that the behaviour named by the test `DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th` passes. That test is NOT present in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour: for the year 1974 in the USA (the year the US switched to year-round DST, Jan 6 1974 - Oct 27 1974), `DateTime#isInDST()` must return true for datetimes within that window.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read the `isInDST` implementation in /luxon/src/datetime.js, and the surrounding offset/zone machinery (/luxon/src/zone.js, /luxon/src/impl/zoneUtil.js, /luxon/src/zones/*.js). Also read the existing tests in /luxon/test/datetime/dst.test.js (if present) or wherever `isInDST` is tested, to learn the conventions and the environment (node ICU/tz data).
2. Reproduce the bug: run a throwaway script (e.g. `npx jest -t isInDST` plus a temporary test file placed OUTSIDE /luxon/test, or `node -e` with babel-node) checking e.g. `DateTime.fromISO('1974-06-01T12:00', { zone: 'America/New_York' }).isInDST()` and the boundary dates Jan 6 1974 / Oct 27 1974, plus a normal year like 2018 for regression. Note the actual vs expected values.
3. Diagnose the root cause. A common shape of this bug: `isInDST` compares the current offset against the offset of the same instant shifted by a fixed number of months (e.g. `this.set({ month: this.month + 6 })` or `this.plus({ months: 6 })`), which is wrong for a year where DST lasts almost the whole year (1974 USA), or it uses `this.offset > this.set({month: 1}).offset` style comparisons that break. Fix it so that DST detection is correct for such years while keeping all other behaviour identical.
4. Keep the fix minimal and general (no special-casing of 1974). Do not change public API beyond the bug.
5. Verify: run `npx jest` from /luxon and confirm all pre-existing tests pass (record pass/fail counts before and after). Also run `npx jest test/datetime`.

CONSTRAINTS: Never edit or delete anything under /luxon/test. Do not run `npm install` or use the network. Do not leave temporary files behind. Do not reformat unrelated code.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, the reproduction (actual vs expected) before the fix, commands run, jest pass/fail counts before and after, and any residual uncertainty (e.g. if the container's tz database does not have the 1974 rule).

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js so that the behaviour named by the test `DateTime#toISODate() correctly pads negative years` passes. That test is NOT present in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour: for a DateTime with a negative (BCE) year, `toISODate()` must produce a correctly padded ISO date string, e.g. year -50 -> `-0050-01-01` (4-digit zero-padded year with a leading minus sign), year -1 -> `-0001-...`, and positive years unchanged (`0050-01-01`, `2017-05-15`).

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js (especially any `padStart`/`padStart`-like helper and any `toISODate`/`toISO` formatting helper), plus /luxon/src/datetime.js `toISODate`, `toISO`, `toISOWeekDate`, `toISOTime`, and /luxon/src/impl/formatter.js if relevant. Find the padding helper used for the year.
2. Reproduce the bug with a throwaway script (e.g. `npx babel-node` one-liner, or a temporary jest test file placed OUTSIDE /luxon/test that you DELETE afterwards). Check: `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -50, month: 1, day: 1 }, { zone: 'utc' }).toISODate()`, `year: -1`, `year: -1234`, `year: 50`, `year: 2017`, and also `toISO()` and `toISOTime()` for the same values. Record actual vs expected.
3. Fix the root cause in /luxon/src/impl/util.js with a minimal, general change (e.g. the padding helper must handle negative numbers by padding the absolute value and re-prefixing the sign, and must not produce `-50-01-01` or `--0050-...`). Do not special-case individual test inputs. Do not change unrelated behaviour, and do not touch other files unless the root cause genuinely is not in util.js (report if so).
4. Verify: run `npx jest` from /luxon and confirm all pre-existing tests still pass (record pass/fail counts before and after your change; note that 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js are expected and unrelated). Also run `npx jest test/datetime`.

CONSTRAINTS: Never edit or delete anything under /luxon/test. Do not run `npm install` or use the network. Do not leave temporary files behind. Do not reformat unrelated code. Do not touch /luxon/src/interval.js, /luxon/src/datetime.js, or /luxon/src/duration.js (other subagents own those).

REPORT BACK: the exact diff you applied, the reproduction (actual vs expected) before the fix, commands run, jest pass/fail counts before and after, whether you had to merge with another subagent's concurrent change in util.js, and any residual uncertainty.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js so that the behaviours named by these two tests pass (neither test is present in the repo; their names describe the expected behaviour):
  1. `A DateTime in an invalid FixedOffsetZone is itself invalid`
  2. `FixedOffsetZone is invalid when constructed with a non-numeric offset`

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js in full, plus /luxon/src/zone.js, /luxon/src/zones/ianaZone.js (or similar), /luxon/src/zones/invalidZone.js, /luxon/src/impl/zoneUtil.js, and the existing tests /luxon/test/zones/fixedOffsetZone.test.js (and any other test that constructs fixed-offset zones) to learn the conventions.
2. Diagnose: the likely bug is that `FixedOffsetZone.instance(offset)` (and/or `parseZone`/`FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance`/`FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier`) accepts a non-numeric offset (e.g. `"blorp"`, `NaN`, `undefined`, an object) and returns a *valid* zone whose `offset()` is NaN, so `DateTime` built in it is not invalid. The expected behaviour: constructing a FixedOffsetZone with a non-numeric offset yields a zone with `isValid === false` (and `DateTime.fromObject(..., { zone: thatZone })` / `DateTime.local().setZone(thatZone)` is invalid, `isValid === false`, `invalidReason` set), while numeric offsets (including 0, negative, and numeric strings like "+3"/"-5" if the existing code supports them) keep working exactly as before.
3. Reproduce first with a throwaway script (e.g. `npx babel-node -e` or a temporary jest file placed OUTSIDE /luxon/test that you DELETE afterwards). Record actual vs expected for: `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp").isValid`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(NaN).isValid`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(undefined).isValid`, `DateTime.fromObject({year:2017}, {zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")}).isValid`, and the same with numeric offsets 0, 3, -5, 5.5 to prove no regression.
4. Fix the root cause with a minimal, general change in /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js only. Follow the conventions of the other zone classes (see how invalidZone.js / ianaZone.js expose `isValid`, and how `Zone`/`DateTime` handle an invalid zone - check `DateTime.setZone` and the DateTime constructor's zone validation so your fix integrates). Do not special-case test inputs, do not add features, do not change unrelated behaviour.
5. Verify: run `npx jest` from /luxon and confirm all pre-existing tests still pass (record pass/fail counts before and after; note that 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js are expected and unrelated). Also run `npx jest test/zones` and `npx jest test/datetime`.

CONSTRAINTS: Never edit or delete anything under /luxon/test. Do not run `npm install` or use the network. Do not leave temporary files behind. Do not reformat unrelated code.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, the reproduction (actual vs expected) before the fix, commands run, jest pass/fail counts before and after, and any residual uncertainty.

GOAL: Fix a bug in /luxon/src/impl/util.js so that the behaviour named by the test `DateTime#plus works across the 100 barrier when passing through February` passes. That test is NOT present in the repo; its name describes the expected behaviour: adding e.g. years/months to a DateTime whose year is 99 (or crossing year 100) while the month arithmetic passes through February must produce the correct result. The likely culprit is a 2-digit-year heuristic in util.js (e.g. a function like `parseTwoDigitYear`, `isUndefined`, `numberBetween`, `integerBetween`, `padStart`, or the `isLeapYear`/`daysInMonth` helpers) that mis-handles year values >= 100 or the year 100 boundary.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /luxon/src/impl/util.js in full, plus /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js, /luxon/src/datetime.js (the `plus`, `set`, `normalizeUnit`/`objToTS` paths) and /luxon/src/impl/gregorian.js if present, to find where a 100 barrier could arise. Look especially for any code that treats years < 100 specially (e.g. `if (year < 100) year += 1900` style logic, or `Math.floor(year / 100)`-based century math, or a `parseTwoDigitYear`-style function that is applied to already-4-digit years).
2. Reproduce the bug first with a small throwaway script (e.g. `node -e` after `npx babel-node`, or a temporary jest test you DELETE afterwards, or `npx jest -t '...'` with a temp test file placed OUTSIDE /luxon/test). Example checks to try: `DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 1, day: 31}).plus({months: 1})`, `DateTime.fromObject({year: 100, month: 1, day: 31}).plus({months: 1})`, `DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 12, day: 31}).plus({months: 2})`, `DateTime.fromObject({year: 99, month: 1, day: 31}).plus({years: 1})`, and the same with `set({year: 100})`. Compare against the correct Gregorian arithmetic (Feb 28/29 handling).
3. Fix the root cause in /luxon/src/impl/util.js (or, only if the root cause genuinely lives elsewhere, in the single other source file that contains it - but the hint says util.js). Keep the fix minimal and general: do not special-case a single test input. Do not change public API behaviour beyond the bug.
4. Verify: run `npx jest` from /luxon and make sure all pre-existing tests still pass (record the pass/fail counts before and after your change). Also run `npx jest test/datetime`.

CONSTRAINTS: Never edit or delete anything under /luxon/test. Do not run `npm install` or use the network. Do not leave temporary files behind. Do not reformat unrelated code.

REPORT BACK: the exact diff, the reproduction you observed before the fix (with actual vs expected values), the commands you ran, jest pass/fail counts before and after, and any residual uncertainty.
